- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day average), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 14-day moving average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; add 1–3 days of smoothing or use 7-day weighted average to align with true trend.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after 3–5 consecutive days above 80), model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is negative or neutral, model often overestimates early in horizon; reduce first 5–7 days by 3–7% to reflect sentiment drag.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 or 0.27 values, model tends to underestimate; add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for suppressed sentiment effect.
